doc: a cooled block: a solid skin with a gyroid sheet lattice filling the core

header: A cooled block: a solid skin with a gyroid sheet lattice filling the core.
part = skin  U  ( core  n  sheet )
hull   the outside shape
core   hull shrunk by the skin thickness       offset(hull, -skin_t)
skin   hull with the core removed              difference(hull, core)
sheet  the gyroid, walled to `wall`            shell(tpms, wall/2)
infill the sheet, CONFINED to the core         intersect(core, sheet)
WHY `intersect` AND NOT A MASK.  A TPMS fills all of R^3 -- `tpms.aabb()`
returns None, and it means it.  `intersect` (a max) is what confines it, and
because max of two BOUND fields is BOUND, the result can still be offset,
sphere-traced and pruned during meshing.  The `mask` node would also work and
is honestly declared IMPLICIT, which costs all of that.
WHY THE TPMS IS `normalise: "proven"`.  The literature's gyroid formula
sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x is IMPLICIT: right sign, right zero
set, no distance.  Dividing it by the family's PROVEN bound on |grad g| makes
it 1-Lipschitz, and a 1-Lipschitz field is a BOUND -- |f| <= dist(x, surface)
everywhere, with no measurement.  Set `normalise` to "none" and you get the
literature's function and IMPLICIT with it; `implexity model show` will say so.
THE WALL IS A FRACTION OF THE CELL.  `wall = period * wall_frac` states the
relationship an engineer actually holds: a lattice at 30 % of its cell is the
same lattice at 4 mm and at 8 mm.  Edit `period` alone and the wall follows.
A WARNING YOU WILL SEE, AND WHY IT IS LEFT IN
`implexity model validate` reports
parameter(s) wall_frac are declared and nothing binds to them
It is wrong.  `wall_frac` is read by the derived parameter `wall`, which a
node does bind; document.py's unused check (`_bound_names`) walks NODE
bindings only and does not follow one named parameter into another's
expression.  The check is one line from being right.  The model is not
restructured to dodge it, and the warning is not suppressed, because a
diagnostic you have quietly routed around is worse than one that is wrong
out loud.
TRY
implexity model show    models/03_lattice_block.json
implexity model eval    models/03_lattice_block.json --node cells --grid 24
implexity model set     models/03_lattice_block.json period=6.0 -o /tmp/coarse.json
implexity model export  models/03_lattice_block.json -o /tmp/block.stl --spacing 0.35
-- a lattice needs a fine grid: the sampling has to resolve the wall, and
the wall here is 1.5 mm.  0.35 mm gives four samples across it.
